back: Many small, fast transactions touching a few rows; row stores like Postgres.
Analytical queries scanning millions of rows over a few columns; column stores like BigQuery.
Each row's values stored together; fast single-row access.
Each column's values stored together; fast scans of a few columns.
Similar values sit together: dictionary and run-length encoding.
Slow single-row updates; writes are batched.
ETL transforms before loading; ELT loads raw data and transforms inside the warehouse.
Change data capture: stream every change from the database log to other systems.
A large fact table of events joined to small dimension tables.
Structured, cleaned tables queried with SQL, storage and compute managed together.
Raw files (often Parquet) in object storage, queried by many engines.
Table formats (Iceberg, Delta, Hudi) adding transactions and schemas to lake files.
Time partitioning, delta compression, downsampling, retention policies, time functions.
Keeping lower-resolution aggregates for older data.
